Bloomberg today published a new in-depth report analyzing Apple's Mac product line. The report details update plans for multiple products over the coming years, including the MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, and iMac.

New MacBook Air, iMac, MacBook Pro, and more

Bloomberg says Apple is aiming to launch the following new Macs before the end of this year:

  • A brand new entry-level MacBook Pro with an M6 chip
  • A brand new iMac
  • A new high-end 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook lineup with touch, powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max, featuring OLED displays

The report says the new high-end MacBook models are "expected to launch between late this year and early next year." Apple is testing these new machines with macOS 27.1, which is expected to release in late October.

Apple plans to launch an updated MacBook Air lineup in early 2027. The company is also working on a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro with an M7 chip, expected next year.

A new MacBook Neo is also in development, with Apple testing a model featuring an A19 Pro chip. The report says Apple plans to release "regular" color refreshes for the MacBook Neo.

Apple is also testing a Mac mini lineup with M5 Pro and base M6 processors. New Mac Studio models with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors are also in testing. Bloomberg cautions: "But the launch timing of these products — as well as the planned chip and memory configurations — will depend on memory chip supply."

Looking further ahead, Bloomberg notes that an OLED MacBook Air is in development, expected to arrive "as early as 2028." An OLED iMac is also reportedly in the works, to follow the OLED MacBook Air.

What are your thoughts on Apple's Mac roadmap? Planning an upgrade? Let us know in the comments.
